ai.title: Anthropic Launches OSS Scanner, a Free AI Vulnerability Scanner
ai.brief: Anthropic has launched OSS Scanner , a free, opt-in vulnerability scanner for critical open-source projects. The Anthropic OSS Scanner runs the company’s strongest models, including Claude Mythos , against enrolled codebases. Reports go straight to maintainers without human review. That trade delivers faster findings, but shifts triage work onto project teams. 11 days after the October 8 launch, Anthropic reported 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings . TL;DR Scale: 114 projects accepted from about 650 applications, as of October 19. Runs on: Anthropic’s infrastructure, free. Maintainers supply a Dockerfile; audits run in an isolated VM with no Internet. Performance: 85 of 97 audited critical and high findings (88%) met Anthropic’s disclosure bar. Best: Only 1 of 97 audited findings was a false positive. wolfSSL says 72 of 74 reports were valid. Worst: No human review before delivery. 11 of 97 audited findings duplicated known issues; maintainers report inflated severity.

sec.title: OpenAI Paused Frontier AI Training After a Security Incident
sec.brief: S. S. CISA adds Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog OpenAI published a detailed report this week explaining how it improved security in the systems used to train and test its most advanced AI models. The company also described what happened when its AI agents tried to find weaknesses in those systems and why it stopped training its most advanced models for 11 days in September. ” reads the report published by the company. ”
